title: EXCLUSIVE: Major Political Party Leader In The Balkans Calls For Trump, Putin To Help Him Create New Christian Nation In Europe
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
EXCLUSIVE: Major Political Party Leader In The Balkans Calls For Trump, Putin To Help Him Create New Christian Nation In Europe

‘I beg them’

Actual Article Body:
(Francis Kapper / Daily Caller News Foundation)

BANJA LUKA, BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA — The president of the ruling political party in Republika Srpska, a political entity in Bosnia and Herzegovina, called upon President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin to support the independence of Srpska in an exclusive interview with the Daily Caller News Foundation.

Milorad Dodik, the president of the Alliance of Independent Social Democrats (SNSD), told the DCNF that, if his push for independence is successful, he would consider submitting an application for the new nation to join the 27-member European Union (EU). The interview was held just days before Bosnia and Herzegovina’s general election Sunday.

WATCH:

Dodik is one of a small number of world leaders who simultaneously maintains positive relations with both the United States and Russia. When explicitly asked by the DCNF if he was calling upon Trump and Putin to support the independence of Srpska, Dodik said he was begging for their support in this initiative. (RELATED: Bosnia Heads Into Sunday Election With Country’s Postwar Order Under Strain)

“I call upon them; I beg them,” Dodik told the DCNF through a translator during his interview in the presidential palace. “If they could only allocate five minutes of their precious time to consider the situation here, it would all be clear to them.”

“I think that we deserve that,” Dodik said through the translator. “But if Donald Trump fails to do that, I will still continue to support him.”

While Republika Srpska already functions as a significant political entity inside Bosnia and Herzegovina, internationally recognized independence would allow the would-be small nation to stand itself up rather quickly, Dodik said.

“It would only take 15 minutes for Republika Srpska to start functioning as an independent state,” Dodik told the DCNF.

“We are part of the European family,” Dodik said. “Actually, we [Republika Srpska] stand a better chance of joining the EU because, via Bosnia and Herzegovina, I don’t think it’s going to happen.”

Dodik previously called for the independence of Republika Srpska in another exclusive interview with the DCNF.

“We are the people who need our freedom and liberty,” Dodik previously told the DCNF through a translator. “And we deserve our freedom and liberty.”

“And that would be the great, historical act of President Trump in the Balkans: to support our liberty, freedom and independence,” Dodik previously told the DCNF. “In the history of Serbs, then, he would become one of the most prominent figures.”

Željka Cvijanović, the current Serb member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the former president of Republika Srpska from 2018 to 2022, seemed to join Dodik’s call for independence during a political rally Friday night, mentioning how Srpska needs “the right to a referendum,” according to a translation of her speech.

The government of Bosnia and Herzegovina features an incredibly complex system of leaders and regional representatives. Formed under the 1995 Dayton Accords, the country primarily consists of two entities, Republika Srpska and the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It has three presidents — a Bosniac, a Croat, and a Serb — while Republika Srpska has its own president.

Cvijanović and Marinko Božović are competing for the Serb seat in Bosnia and Herzegovina’s three-member presidency. Cvijanović is running on behalf of the ruling SNSD and is closely aligned with Dodik.

Given the history of wars throughout the countries that comprise the now-defunct state of Yugoslavia, the DCNF asked if Dodik could commit to a peaceful secession from Bosnia and Herzegovina. Dodik agreed, saying it was the only way forward.

(Francis Kapper / Daily Caller News Foundation)
